name: GitHub
description: What GitHub itself reads out of the repository: the Actions workflows in `.github/workflows`, read as they are written, and the CODEOWNERS file, read as rules. For a workflow, which events start it, what token permissions it hands a job, which runner each job asks for, and every action a step reaches for and how tightly it is pinned. For CODEOWNERS, every pattern in file order with the owners it names, and the owners that apply to the paths a guardrail asks about, resolved the way GitHub resolves them, where the last rule to match a path is the one that owns it. Names and shapes only, never a secret, an input value or an environment value.

workflows.description: Comma separated globs matched against every file in the working directory and against bare file names, naming the workflows to read. Narrows what discovery finds; a file it matches that is not under `.github/workflows` is still left out.

paths.description: Comma separated paths to resolve owners for, relative to the repository root. A guardrail that cares about the files a pull request changed names them here.

facts.source: `report` when a workflow or a CODEOWNERS file was read, `none` when neither was.
facts.reason: Why nothing was read, present only when `source` is `none`.
facts.reports: Every file that was read, workflows in path order and the CODEOWNERS file after them.
facts.reports[].path: Path of the workflow, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.
facts.reports[].modified: When it was last written, ISO 8601.
facts.reports[].format: `workflow` for an Actions workflow, `codeowners` for the CODEOWNERS file.
facts.workflows: The workflows themselves, one entry per file that was read. Absent when the repository carries none, so a check reads its absence rather than an empty list.
facts.workflows[].path: Path of the file, relative to the directory the CLI runs in.
facts.workflows[].name: Name the workflow gives itself, or `null` when it names none.
facts.workflows[].triggers: The `on` keys: the events that start the workflow.
facts.workflows[].permissions: The workflow level `permissions` value, exactly as written. `null` when the file declares none, in which case the token gets the repository's default permissions, not an empty set.
facts.workflows[].defaults: The workflow level `defaults` value, exactly as written. `null` when there is none.
facts.workflows[].concurrency: Whether the file declares a workflow level concurrency group, so an in flight run is cancelled or queued rather than racing.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].id: Key the job is declared under, which is what `needs` names.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].name: Display name the job gives itself, or `null`.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].runsOn: The `runs-on` value, exactly as written: a label, a list of labels or a runner group.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].selfHosted: `false` when the runner is one of GitHub's hosted images, `true` when it is explicitly `self-hosted` or names no hosted image, and `null` when the label is an expression.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].permissions: The job level `permissions` value, exactly as written. `null` when the job declares none and inherits whatever the workflow or the repository gives it.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].timeoutMinutes: The declared `timeout-minutes`, exactly as written, or `null` when the job declares none and takes GitHub's six hour default.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].environment: The deployment environment the job runs in, exactly as written, or `null`. An environment is what carries a protection rule and its own secrets.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].if: The raw condition guarding the job, or `null`.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].uses: The reusable workflow this job calls instead of declaring steps, exactly as written, or `null`.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].secretsUsed: Names of the secrets referenced anywhere in the job, and the keys of a `secrets` block it passes on. Names only, never values: the facts are attached to the run event.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].steps: The steps the job declares, in order.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].steps[].name: Display name of the step, or `null`.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].steps[].uses: The action the step runs, exactly as written, or `null` for a step that only runs a script.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].steps[].action: The part of `uses` before the `@`: `owner/repo` with any subdirectory for a published action, the path for a `./` local action, the image for a `docker://` action.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].steps[].ref: What follows the `@` in `uses`, whatever it names, or `null` when it names nothing. Apart from `pinned`, a tag, a branch and a sha look the same here.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].steps[].pinned: Whether `ref` is a 40 character hex commit sha, which is the only ref a tag cannot be moved out from under.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].steps[].local: Whether the action is a `./` path in this repository rather than a published one.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].steps[].docker: Whether the action is a `docker://` image rather than a published one.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].steps[].run: The shell body the step runs, truncated to 2000 characters, or `null`.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].steps[].shell: The shell the step declares for itself, or `null` when it takes the default the workflow or GitHub sets.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].steps[].withKeys: Names of the inputs the step passes to the action. Names only, never values.
facts.workflows[].jobs[].steps[].interpolation: Every `${{ }}` expression appearing in the `run` body, read from the whole body before it was truncated. An expression interpolated into a shell body is the script injection surface.
facts.triggers: Every event declared across the workflows that were read.
facts.untrustedTriggers: One entry per workflow and trigger that runs with the repository's own token on a change written by somebody outside the repository: `pull_request_target`, `issue_comment` and `workflow_run`.
facts.untrustedTriggers[].path: Path of the workflow declaring it.
facts.unparsed: Files that matched but were not read, because their YAML uses something outside the subset the collector can represent. A file listed here is not an empty file: nothing was read from it, so draw no verdict about it.
facts.unparsed[].path: Path of the file that was not read.
facts.unparsed[].reason: The construct that could not be represented, and the line it is on.
facts.codeowners: The CODEOWNERS file the repository carries. Absent when it carries none at any of the three locations GitHub reads one from, so a check reads its absence rather than an empty rule list.
facts.codeowners.path: Path of the CODEOWNERS file that was read: the first of `.github/CODEOWNERS`, `CODEOWNERS` and `docs/CODEOWNERS` that exists, which is the order GitHub searches them in. A repository carrying more than one of them is owned by the first, and the rest are text GitHub never reads.
facts.codeowners.rules: Every rule the file declares, in file order, which is the order GitHub resolves them in.
facts.codeowners.rules[].pattern: Pattern exactly as it is written, so an anchored `/docs/` reads differently from a `docs/` matched at any depth. A bracketed line such as `[Docs]` is a pattern too, not a heading: GitHub CODEOWNERS has no section headers, so the line is resolved like any other rule and owns whatever it matches.
facts.codeowners.rules[].owners: Owners the rule names, as GitHub users (`@dana`), GitHub teams (`@company/platform`) or email addresses. Empty when the rule names none, which removes ownership from everything it matches.
facts.codeowners.rules[].line: Line the rule is declared on, so a verdict points at the file.
facts.codeowners.owners: Every owner the file names, by owner, with how many rules name them.
facts.codeowners.matched: Owners GitHub resolves for each path the `paths` input named, by the path exactly as it was given. A path nobody asked about is absent, so read the ones the guardrail configured rather than iterating.
facts.codeowners.matched[path].owners: Owners the last rule to match names, because the last match is what GitHub gives the path. Empty when no rule matched, and empty when the last one to match names no owners.
facts.codeowners.matched[path].rule: Pattern of the last rule that matched, or `null` when none did.
facts.codeowners.matched[path].line: Line that rule is declared on, or `null` when none matched.
facts.codeowners.unparsed: Every line that is not a rule, in file order. Comments and blank lines are not among them, because GitHub ignores them rather than misreading them.
facts.codeowners.unparsed[].line: Line that could not be read as a rule.
facts.codeowners.unparsed[].reason: Why it could not be read as one.
